Scenario: A delegation the case officer has not accepted does not run.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1. Delta: the case officer has no Case assistant delegation yet | 2. As the Owner, set up a Case assistant delegation for the case officer | 3. The case officer does not accept it | 4. As Client A, upload a document on Case C-1 (a trigger of the Case assistant's recipes) | 5. Open the delegation record and Case C-1's run list
Expected Result: The delegation state is PENDING_ACCEPTANCE; no persona recipe runs for the case officer's files.
Comments: US-1; AW-1-5; AW-1-6. Counsel: CQ4 (privacy), CQ1 (regulatory), CQ13a.

Scenario: An accepted delegation with the assistant switched on becomes active and its run opens.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1. Delta: the case officer has no Case assistant delegation yet | 2. As the Owner, set up a Case assistant delegation for the case officer | 3. As the case officer, accept it | 4. As Client A, upload a document on Case C-1 (a trigger of the Case assistant's recipes) | 5. Open the delegation record, the run list and the audit log
Expected Result: The delegation is ACTIVE with acceptedAt filled; the run opens on Case C-1; both the set-up and the acceptance are in the audit log.
Comments: US-1; AW-1-5; AW-1-6. Counsel: CQ4 (privacy), CQ1 (regulatory), CQ13a.

Scenario: A delegation accepted while the Case assistant's switch is still off is paused until the Owner switches it on.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1. Delta: the case officer has no Case assistant delegation yet; the Case assistant's switch is off (its default) | 2. As the Owner, set up a Case assistant delegation for the case officer | 3. As the case officer, accept it | 4. As Client A, upload a document on Case C-1 (a trigger of the Case assistant's recipes) | 5. Check the delegation and the run list | 6. As the Owner, switch the Case assistant on | 7. Check the delegation again
Expected Result: After the upload the delegation is PAUSED with ASSISTANT_SWITCH_OFF and no run opens; after the switch-on the delegation is ACTIVE with no new acceptance.
Comments: US-1; AW-1-6; AW-1-11; AW-1-125; AG-16-59. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ13a.

Scenario: An Admin cannot set up a delegation for another person.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-ADMIN, FX-F-CO. Delta: the case officer has no Case assistant delegation yet | 2. As the firm Admin, try to set up a Case assistant delegation for the case officer on screen | 3. As the firm Admin, repeat the set-up as a direct request to the server
Expected Result: Both attempts are refused; no delegation record is created.
Comments: US-1; AW-1-6. Negative test. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ13a.

Scenario: No one but the named person can end an active delegation.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-ADMIN, FX-F-CO | 2. As the Owner, look for an action that ends the case officer's delegation | 3. As the firm Admin, do the same | 4. As the Owner, send a direct request to end the delegation
Expected Result: No end action is offered to the Owner or the firm Admin and the direct request is refused; the delegation stays ACTIVE. The Owner's only options are to switch the assistant or AI off, or to deactivate or suspend the person.
Comments: US-1; AW-1-6; AW-1-125; AW1-D34. Negative test. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ13a.

Scenario: Keys a Case assistant may never hold are refused at set-up.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO. Delta: the case officer has no Case assistant delegation yet | 2. As the Owner, open the set-up screen of a Case assistant delegation for the case officer | 3. As the Owner, add agent/case:review-approve and save | 4. As the Owner, add agent/sqr:verify and save | 5. As the Owner, add agent/sqr:document-manage and save | 6. As the Owner, add a send key and save | 7. As the Owner, add an export key and save
Expected Result: Each save is refused by the server with the reason; nothing is saved.
Comments: US-2; AW-1-8; AW-1-9; SA-6-53. Negative test. Counsel: CQ13a, CQ3 (regulatory); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: A direct request adding a never-held key to a Case assistant delegation is refused.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO. Delta: the case officer has no Case assistant delegation yet | 2. As the tester, send a direct request (not through the screen) to create a Case assistant delegation for the case officer whose subset includes agent/case:review-approve | 3. Check the delegation records
Expected Result: The server refuses with the reason; no delegation record exists.
Comments: US-2; AW-1-9; AW-1-37. Negative test. Counsel: CQ3 (regulatory), CQ13a; provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: A key outside the Case Officer column of SA-06 v3.3 §10b is refused.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO. Delta: the case officer has no Case assistant delegation yet | 2. As the Owner, set up a Case assistant delegation for the case officer | 3. As the Owner, add a key that is not Y in the Case Officer column of SA-06 v3.6 §10b and save
Expected Result: The key is refused; nothing is saved.
Comments: US-2; AW-1-8; AW-1-9. Negative test. Counsel: CQ13a, CQ3 (regulatory); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: A key not marked lendable is refused.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO. Delta: the case officer has no Case assistant delegation yet | 2. As the Owner, set up a Case assistant delegation for the case officer | 3. As the Owner, add a key that is in the Case Officer column but not marked assistantLendable (SA-6-53) and save
Expected Result: The key is refused; nothing is saved.
Comments: US-2; AW-1-8; AW-1-9; SA-6-53. Negative test. Counsel: CQ13a, CQ3 (regulatory); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: An unlicensed case officer's delegation becomes active and shows the licence fact as information.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO. Delta: the case officer has no Case assistant delegation yet and no linked regulator credential | 2. As the Owner, set up a Case assistant delegation for the case officer | 3. As the case officer, accept it | 4. Open the delegation
Expected Result: The delegation is ACTIVE; it shows 'not linked to a licence' as information only and is not blocked by it.
Comments: US-3; AW-1-7. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ13a.

Scenario: A client draft prepared under an unlicensed officer's delegation waits for a holder of the sending key, who may be unlicensed.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-MODEL. Delta: the case officer is unlicensed and holds `agent/communication:send-email`; the scripted model returns a draft reply with no eligibility statement, legal opinion or deadline promise | 2. As Client A, send a question on Case C-1 | 3. Run the Case assistant on the question | 4. Open the reply item | 5. As the case officer, approve it
Expected Result: The reply waits as an approval item and is not sent before a person approves it. The unlicensed case officer, who holds the sending key, can approve it, and the approval is accepted with no licence check shown or recorded.
Comments: Re-based 14 Oct 2026: the AI-text approver setting and its licensed-only default are withdrawn (AW-1-31 re-based 13 Oct 2026; SA-05 v3.4 R5; SA-06 v3.6 SA6-D14); any holder of the sending key approves (AIW-D134). A draft flagged under AIW-D136 is not covered here. US-3; AW-1-31. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory).

Scenario: Deactivating the case officer ends the delegation and cancels its two waiting drafts.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply to each question | 2. As Client A, send two questions on Case C-1 and run the Case assistant on each, so two drafts wait | 3. As the Owner, deactivate the case officer | 4. Open the delegation, the two drafts and the audit log
Expected Result: The delegation is ENDED with reason DEACTIVATED at the next safe point; no step was stopped mid-send; both drafts are cancelled with DELEGATION_ENDED and remain visible in the audit.
Comments: US-4; AW-1-11; AW-1-20; AG-11-113. Counsel: CQ13a.

Scenario: Reactivating a person does not restore their ended delegation.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO. Delta: the Owner has deactivated the case officer and the case officer's delegation is ENDED | 2. As the Owner, reactivate the case officer | 3. As the case officer, open the Case assistant
Expected Result: The old delegation stays ENDED; a new delegation must be set up and accepted before the assistant works.
Comments: US-4; AW-1-11; CN-AG-01 change 2. Counsel: CQ13a.

Scenario: The Firm assistant offers only the Owner and the Case Manager as delegators.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CM, FX-F-ADMIN | 2. As the Owner, open the Firm assistant's settings | 3. As the Owner, start setting up delegations and look at the delegator choices
Expected Result: Only the Owner and the Case Manager can be chosen; the firm Admin is not offered.
Comments: US-5; AW-1-12. Counsel: CQ13a.

Scenario: The Owner's and the Case Manager's Firm assistant delegations are separate records.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CM. Delta: neither the Owner nor the Case Manager has a Firm assistant delegation | 2. As the Owner, set up a Firm assistant delegation for the Owner and accept it | 3. As the Owner, set up a Firm assistant delegation for the Case Manager; as the Case Manager, accept it | 4. Open both delegation records
Expected Result: Two records exist, each with its own subset; nothing is shared between them.
Comments: US-5; AW-1-12. Counsel: CQ13a.

Scenario: A second live delegation for the same person and delegating role is refused.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CM. Delta: the Case Manager's Firm assistant delegation is in state PENDING_ACCEPTANCE | 2. As the Owner, try to set up a second Firm assistant delegation for the Case Manager in the same delegating role | 3. As the Case Manager, accept the first delegation; as the Owner, try again | 4. As the Owner, switch the Firm assistant off so the delegation is PAUSED; try again
Expected Result: Each second set-up is refused; only one live delegation exists for that person, assistant and delegating role.
Comments: US-5; AW-1-12. Negative test. Counsel: CQ13a.

Scenario: A persona recipe at a new version cannot be enabled before its rehearsal.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-PLATFORM, FX-PL-OWNER | 2. As the Platform Owner, publish a new version of the readiness-report recipe | 3. As the Owner (holder of agent/automation:use-recipe and agent/automation:enable), try to enable it before any rehearsal of that version
Expected Result: Enabling is refused.
Comments: US-6; AW-1-13; AW-1-14; AG-11-115. Negative test.

Scenario: After a rehearsal with zero side effects the recipe can be enabled and the settings page shows the rehearsal.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER. Delta: a new version of the readiness-report recipe is published and has no rehearsal yet | 2. As the Owner (holder of agent/automation:simulate), run the rehearsal of the new version | 3. As the Owner, confirm the rehearsal made zero side effects | 4. As the Owner, enable the recipe | 5. As the Owner, open the assistant's settings page and the audit log
Expected Result: Enabling is allowed and audited; the settings page shows the rehearsed version, the date and the person who ran it.

Scenario: A seed's document chase stays a product automation when no assistant exists.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CM, FX-F-BK, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1. Delta: no assistant delegation exists in Firm F (the case officer's, the Case Manager's and the bookkeeper's are not set up) | 2. As the case officer, request a document from Client A on Case C-1 | 3. The firm's wait period passes with the document still missing | 4. Open the sent chase, its audit entry and the run list
Expected Result: The seed's chase is sent; its audit mode is AUTOMATION; no prepared-file count and no persona run exist.

Scenario: The double-run check stops the assistant repeating a chase the seed already sent.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-REQ-X | 2. The seed sends chase 1 of the open request round | 3. Start the Case assistant's run on the same chase | 4. Open Client A's messages and the run record
Expected Result: The engine reports a match on actGuardKey; no second message is sent; the run record holds a skip entry naming the seed run.
Comments: US-8; AW-1-18; AG-11-115. Negative test.

Scenario: A chase in a new request round is not blocked by the double-run check.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-REQ-X. Delta: Client A has uploaded a document for checklist item X, and the seed has already sent chase 1 of round 1 | 2. As the case officer, reject the upload for checklist item X so it is re-requested (a new round) | 3. Start the Case assistant's run on the chase for the new round | 4. Open the run record
Expected Result: The chase for the new round is not blocked by the double-run check: the run record holds no skip entry for it.

Scenario: Starting the assistant again on the same case continues the same run.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1. Delta: a Case assistant run is open on Case C-1 | 2. As the case officer, ask the assistant to start again on Case C-1 | 3. Pause the run (switch the Case assistant off and on), then, as the case officer, ask it to start again | 4. Open the run list
Expected Result: The same run continues each time; no second run record exists for Case C-1.

Scenario: Each audit entry carries the right mode and actor: no person on the AUTOMATION entry, the case officer on the DELEGATED and PERSON entries.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-REQ-X, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply | 2. The seed sends chase 1 of the open request round | 3. A product alert starts a Case assistant draft on Case C-1 | 4. As the case officer, approve the draft | 5. As the Owner (the auditor), read the audit log for Case C-1
Expected Result: The seed chase shows AUTOMATION with no person as actor and the seed's recipe reference; the draft shows DELEGATED with the case officer as actor, the delegation reference, startedBy = PRODUCT_ALERT and the personaRunId; the approval shows PERSON with the case officer as actor and the delegation reference.
Comments: US-10; AW-1-21; AG-13-68 (CN-AG-13 change 2: an AUTOMATION entry names no person as actor). Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ13a.

Scenario: The provenance view lists every AI-prepared item with its run, sources, approver, decision and before and after.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1. Delta: Case C-1 holds AI-prepared Reader values (one a passport number, Restricted), a drafted reply and a readiness report, each approved or rejected by a person | 2. As the case officer, open the AI provenance view of Case C-1
Expected Result: Each AI-prepared item shows its run, sources, approver, decision and before and after; the Restricted value shows its status only.
Comments: US-11; AW-1-23. Counsel: CQ4 (privacy).

Scenario: A user who cannot open the case sees nothing of it in the provenance view.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-BK, FX-F-C1. Delta: Case C-1 holds AI-prepared Reader values, a drafted reply and a readiness report; the bookkeeper has no permission to open Case C-1 | 2. As the bookkeeper, request the provenance view of Case C-1 on screen | 3. As the bookkeeper, request it again by direct request
Expected Result: Nothing of the case is shown or counted.
Comments: US-11; AW-1-23. Negative test. Counsel: CQ4 (privacy).

Scenario: The whole-firm export carries the AI record.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER. Delta: Firm F holds AI run log rows, a provenance view and question records | 2. As the Owner, request the whole-firm export | 3. As the Owner, open the completed export
Expected Result: It contains the AI run log, the provenance view and the question records beside the approval history.
Comments: US-12; AW-1-24; AG-16-39. Counsel: CQ4 (privacy), CQ8, CQ16.

Scenario: An Owner-route approval records the licence fact and the Owner-route wording.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-NOLIC, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply to Client A | 2. As the Owner, switch off the no-licensed-user pause setting (AG-16-58) with a reason | 3. As Client A, send a question on Case C-1 | 4. Run the Case assistant on the question | 5. As the Owner, approve the draft | 6. Open the approval record
Expected Result: The record shows the approver, that the approver was not linked to a credential at the decision, the sending key under which the approver approved, and 'approved by Owner without a licensed user'.
Comments: Re-based 14 Oct 2026: AW-1-26 records the approver's sending key, not the withdrawn AI-text approver setting. US-13; AW-1-26; AG-11-90; AG-11-113. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory).

Scenario: An Owner-route approval adds one to the month's Owner-route count.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-NOLIC, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-MODEL. Delta: the no-licensed-user pause setting (AG-16-58) is switched off; the scripted model returns a draft reply to Client A | 2. As the Owner, open the firm's AI measures and note the month's Owner-route count (AG-14-39) | 3. As Client A, send a question on Case C-1 and run the Case assistant on it | 4. As the Owner, approve the draft by the Owner route | 5. As the Owner, open the firm's AI measures again
Expected Result: The month's Owner-route count has risen by one.

Scenario: A proposed invoice goes to the bookkeeper who delegated, not the file owner.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-BK, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1. Delta: the case officer is the file owner of Case C-1 | 2. Run the Billing assistant on Case C-1, so it creates an INVOICE_PROPOSAL | 3. Open the bookkeeper's and the case officer's Needs you
Expected Result: The proposal appears in the bookkeeper's Needs you and not in the case officer's.
Comments: US-14; AW-1-30. Proposal.

Scenario: An unlicensed user cannot approve an AI-drafted client reply under the default setting.
Steps: 1. Firm F meets the shared preconditions (AI Doers extra, published provider record, AI switch on) | 2. Keep the AI-text approver setting at its default (licensed users only) | 3. Let the Case assistant draft a reply to Client A | 4. As an unlicensed user who holds agent/communication:send-email, try to approve it
Expected Result: The approval is refused.
Comments: Withdrawn 14 Oct 2026: contradicted by AW-1-31 as re-based 13 Oct 2026 (the AI-text approver setting and its licensed-only default are withdrawn: SA-05 v3.4 R5; SA-06 v3.6 SA6-D14) and AIW-D134 (any holder of the sending key approves AI-written client text). Replacement: TC-AW1-011 (re-worded) and TC-AW1-031. Was: US-15; AW-1-31; AG-16-46. Negative test. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory).

Scenario: A licensed user without the send key cannot approve an AI-drafted client reply.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-LIC, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply | 2. As Client A, send a question on Case C-1 | 3. Run the Case assistant on the question | 4. As the licensed staff member, who does not hold agent/communication:send-email, try to approve the reply
Expected Result: The approval is refused and the reply stays waiting.
Comments: Re-based 14 Oct 2026: made self-contained because TC-AW1-030, which it continued, is withdrawn (AW-1-31; AIW-D134: the sending key is what approves). US-15; AW-1-31. Negative test. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory).

Scenario: A licensed approver without the generate key cannot approve a W-06 letter that is filed, not sent.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-F-LIC, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a W-06 letter draft for Case C-1 (to be filed, not sent) | 2. As the case officer, ask inline for a W-06 letter on Case C-1 | 3. As the licensed staff member, who does not hold agent/document:generate, try to approve the letter
Expected Result: The approval is refused and the letter is not filed.
Comments: US-15; AW-1-31; AW-1-84. Negative test. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ2 (regulatory), CQ11.

Scenario: A licensed approver with the generate key approves and files a W-06 letter.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-F-LIC, FX-MODEL. Delta: the licensed staff member holds `agent/document:generate`; the scripted model returns a W-06 letter draft for Case C-1 (to be filed, not sent) | 2. As the case officer, ask inline for a W-06 letter on Case C-1 | 3. As the licensed staff member, approve the letter
Expected Result: The letter is approved and filed.
Comments: US-15; AW-1-31; AW-1-84. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ2 (regulatory), CQ11.

Scenario: The approver is told when values came from client content.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-CM, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns two proposed values from the upload | 2. As Client A, upload a document on Case C-1 | 3. Run the Reader on the upload | 4. As the Case Manager, open the resulting item
Expected Result: One line beside the approve button says the values came from client content.

Scenario: Approve-all stays disabled until every uncertain value has been opened.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY, FX-F-SAFE, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns twenty values for the report, three at confidence 0.60 and seventeen at 0.95 | 2. Start the readiness report build on Case C-1 | 3. As the case officer, open the item
Expected Result: Approve all is disabled and the three values are listed to open.
Comments: US-17; AW-1-33. Negative test. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: Approve-all becomes enabled once each uncertain value has been opened.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY, FX-F-SAFE, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns twenty values for the report, three at confidence 0.60 and seventeen at 0.95; the report is built and open | 2. As the case officer, open each of the three listed values | 3. Check the approve-all button
Expected Result: Approve all becomes enabled.
Comments: US-17; AW-1-33. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: At least one value of a Reader value set is held out for the approver to type.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CM, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a Reader value set of twenty values on Case C-1, none Restricted | 2. Start the readiness report build on Case C-1 | 3. As the Case Manager, open the item | 4. As the Case Manager, type the held-out value | 5. Inspect the HoldoutCheck record
Expected Result: At least one value is shown blank for typing; a HoldoutCheck records matched or not, and does not store the value.
Comments: US-18; AW-1-33. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: An agreement alarm is shown to the approver alone.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CM, FX-F-SAFE. Delta: ten proposals wait for the Case Manager | 2. As the Case Manager, approve all ten proposals without edits within the alarm window | 3. The alarm window of one hour closes | 4. As the Case Manager, open the Case Manager's screen
Expected Result: An AgreementAlarm is shown to the Case Manager.
Comments: US-19; AW-1-33; AG-11-49. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: No other person can see whose agreement alarm it was.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CM, FX-F-C1, FX-F-SAFE. Delta: an AgreementAlarm has been raised for the Case Manager | 2. As the Owner, open Needs you, the firm's AI measures, Advanced settings, the provenance view of Case C-1 and the audit viewer | 3. As the case officer, open the same screens
Expected Result: No alarm naming that approver is visible; the firm's AI measures show only the firm-wide count of alarms.
Comments: US-19; AW-1-33; AG-14-39. Negative test. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: With the pause setting on and no licensed user, no new client reply is drafted but internal work continues.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CM, FX-MODEL. Delta: the no-licensed-user pause setting (AG-16-58) is on; the Owner holds no licence link, so the Case Manager is the only licensed user; one AI-drafted reply waits on Case C-1; the scripted model returns a draft reply to any question | 2. As the Owner, deactivate the Case Manager, the only licensed user | 3. As Client A, send a new question on Case C-1 | 4. Open Case C-1's drafts, tasks and waiting items
Expected Result: No new reply is drafted; internal tasks are still created; the waiting reply stays PENDING under AG-11-88 and AG-11-90's approval rule.
Comments: US-20; AW-1-34; AW-1-20; AG-16-58. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: With the pause setting switched off with a reason, a draft is prepared and can reach the Owner route.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CM, FX-MODEL. Delta: the no-licensed-user pause setting (AG-16-58) is on and the Case Manager, the only licensed user, is deactivated; the scripted model returns a draft reply to any question | 2. As the Owner, switch the AG-16-58 setting off with a reason | 3. As Client A, send a new question on Case C-1 | 4. Run the Case assistant on the question | 5. Open the new draft and the audit log
Expected Result: A draft is prepared and can reach the Owner route; the switch-off is audited with its reason.
Comments: US-20; AW-1-34; AG-11-90. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: With no second-approver setting in the product, the delegating officer who prepared a form may approve it alone, recorded Self-approved (AIW-D157).
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CM, FX-F-C1. Delta: the product has no second-approver setting (SR-Q1c); the case officer and the Case Manager both hold `agent/case:form-approve` | 2. As the case officer, ask the Case assistant to prepare a form draft on Case C-1 | 3. Open the draft and check it waits for an explicit approval | 4. As the case officer, approve it
Expected Result: preparedByUserId is the case officer and preparedByDelegationId is the delegation; the draft waits for an explicit approval; the case officer's approval is accepted with no second approver asked and is recorded 'Self-approved'.
Comments: Re-based 14 Oct 2026 (AIW-D157): the founder dropped the second-approver half of AIW-D128 because the team removed the Team safeguards switch and two-person approval for firms (SR-Q1c; shared Overview v3.11 L125; SA-06 v3.6 SA6-X11). US-21; AW-1-35; AG-7-66; AG-07 BR-24. Unconfirmed: no counsel (AIW-D94).

Scenario: Where the firm has one form approver, the delegating officer is recorded as the form's preparer and may approve it as Self-approved.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1. Delta: the case officer is the only holder of `agent/case:form-approve` | 2. As the case officer, ask the Case assistant to prepare a form draft on Case C-1 | 3. Open the draft | 4. As the case officer, approve it
Expected Result: preparedByUserId is the case officer and preparedByDelegationId is the delegation; the draft waits for the case officer's explicit approval; the approval is recorded 'Self-approved'.
Comments: Re-based 14 Oct 2026: AW-1-35 as decided by AIW-D128 (one form approver may approve their own assistant's form draft, recorded 'Self-approved', AG-7-66; every form still waits for a person's explicit approval, AG-07 BR-24). US-21; AW-1-35. Unconfirmed: no counsel (AIW-D94).

Scenario: An assistant's draft never sends because its due time passed.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply; a draft's due time is 24 hours after it is prepared | 2. As Client A, send a question on Case C-1 | 3. Run the Case assistant on the question | 4. 24 hours pass; the draft's due time passes with no decision | 5. Open the draft
Expected Result: The draft is marked overdue and escalated; nothing is sent.
Comments: US-22; AW-1-36; AG-11-59. Negative test.

Scenario: A crafted request for a blocked action is refused on the server and the run continues.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-F-DOC1. Delta: a Case assistant run is open on Case C-1 | 2. As the tester, bypassing the screens, send a crafted request asking the engine to delete Document D-1 | 3. Open the action result and the run
Expected Result: The server refuses; the action result names the limit hit; the run continues.
Comments: US-23; AW-1-37; AG-11-28; Hard limit enforcement (AW-1-37). Negative test. Counsel: CQ3 (regulatory); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: No assistant deletes or disposes of a document, note, case or client.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-DOC1, FX-MODEL. Delta: a Case assistant run is open on Case C-1; the scripted model returns, one after another, calls to delete Document D-1, dispose of Document D-1, delete a note, delete Case C-1 and delete Client A | 2. Run the next step of the Case assistant's run | 3. Open the run record
Expected Result: Each attempt is refused and recorded.
Comments: US-24; AW-1-38; Hard limit AW-1-38 (no deleting). Negative test.

Scenario: Approving a proposed invoice creates no invoice record until the bookkeeper saves.
Steps: 1. Firm F meets the shared preconditions (AI Doers extra, published provider record, AI switch on) | 2. Let the Billing assistant create an INVOICE_PROPOSAL for Client B | 3. As the bookkeeper, approve it so the builder opens | 4. Check invoices before saving | 5. Save as the bookkeeper
Expected Result: Before the save no invoice record, draft or number exists; the draft exists only after the bookkeeper saves.
Comments: Withdrawn 12 Oct 2026: contradicted by AIW-D103 (12 Oct 2026; AIW-D44 superseded): an approved invoice proposal now creates the invoice as previewed. Replacement: TC-AW1-268. Was: US-25; AW-1-39; AW-1-101; AG-6-45. Counsel: CQ9 (regulatory).

Scenario: Any assistant call to make a money or trust entry is refused.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-BK, FX-MODEL. Delta: a Billing assistant run is open; the scripted model returns, one after another, calls to create a payment, a refund, a credit and a trust entry, set and move a funds designation, record a trust-to-operating move and a bank position, and run the reconciliation report | 2. Run the next steps of the Billing assistant's run | 3. Open the run record
Expected Result: Every call is refused.
Comments: 12 Oct 2026: still valid under AIW-D103, which keeps "AI cannot grant itself permissions or bypass product controls": a direct act by the assistant is refused; preparing the act for a person's approval is tested in TC-AW1-268 to TC-AW1-275. AW-1-37 as amended; AW-1-141(c) (was AW-1-39, US-25); AG-6-47; Hard limit AW-1-39 (no money or trust entry). Negative test. Counsel: CQ9 (regulatory).

Scenario: No assistant output carries a trust list or a trust figure.
Steps: 1. Firm F meets the shared preconditions (AI Doers extra, published provider record, AI switch on) | 2. Let every Billing assistant duty run for Firm F (W-12a to W-12d, W-27 and the money note) | 3. Inspect every output
Expected Result: No output carries a trust list or a trust figure.
Comments: Withdrawn 12 Oct 2026: contradicted by AIW-D103 (12 Oct 2026; AIW-D72 amended): a proposed trust entry's preview carries its computed amount. Replacement: TC-AW1-271. Was: US-25; AW-1-39; AW-1-100; AW-1-102; Hard limit AW-1-39. Negative test. Counsel: CQ9 (regulatory).

Scenario: The Firm assistant never generates the per-individual export package.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-MODEL. Delta: the Owner has an ACTIVE Firm assistant delegation; the scripted model returns a drafted reply to a privacy request and a call to generate the per-individual package | 2. As Client A, submit a privacy request | 3. Run the Firm assistant on the privacy request | 4. Check whether a per-individual package exists | 5. As the Owner, run the export under agent/data-export:request
Expected Result: The assistant generates no package; the package exists only after the Owner's act.
Comments: US-26; AW-1-40; AW-1-107; Hard limit AW-1-40 (no export). Negative test. Counsel: CQ4 (privacy), CQ8, CQ16.

Scenario: No assistant changes people, roles, settings or switches.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-MODEL. Delta: a Case assistant run is open; the scripted model returns, one after another, calls to change a role, the AI switch, an assistant's switch, the Escalation and At-risk marks settings, an autonomy level, a recipe's state and a safeguard value | 2. Run the next steps of the Case assistant's run | 3. Open the run record
Expected Result: Each attempt is refused and recorded.
Comments: Re-based 14 Oct 2026: the Escalation and At-risk marks settings replaced Team safeguards, supervision and the AI-text approver setting (AW-1-41). US-27; AW-1-41; Hard limit AW-1-41 (no change to people, roles, settings or switches). Negative test.

Scenario: The Intake assistant takes no signing or retainer action.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-INTAKE, FX-F-L1, FX-MODEL. Delta: a retainer awaits countersignature on Lead L-1; an Intake assistant run is open on Lead L-1; the scripted model returns, one after another, an e-signature action and calls to generate, edit, approve for sending and send a retainer | 2. Start the Intake assistant's next step on Lead L-1 | 3. Open Lead L-1's retainer and the run record
Expected Result: No e-signature action is taken and no retainer is generated, edited, approved for sending or sent.
Comments: US-28; AW-1-42; Hard limit AW-1-42 (no signing, no retainer). Negative test.

Scenario: No assistant passes a finding, verifies a value or records a milestone.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-MODEL. Delta: Case C-1 has a CRITICAL finding and unverified values; the scripted model returns, one after another, calls to pass the finding, verify a value, mark a document Verified and record a milestone | 2. Run the next steps of the Case assistant's run on Case C-1 | 3. Open the run record
Expected Result: Each attempt is refused.
Comments: US-29; AW-1-43; Hard limit AW-1-43 (no professional approval or verification). Negative test. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory).

Scenario: The Intake assistant never moves a lead to WON, LOST or any stage.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-INTAKE, FX-F-L1, FX-MODEL. Delta: Lead L-1 has a signed retainer; the scripted model proposes moving Lead L-1 to WON | 2. Start the Intake assistant's run on Lead L-1 | 3. Open Lead L-1's stage and the audit trail
Expected Result: Lead L-1's stage is unchanged and the audit trail shows no stage move by the assistant.
Comments: US-30; AW-1-44; Hard limit AW-1-44 (no stage moves). Negative test.

Scenario: The Intake assistant can only propose a stage move for the rep.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-INTAKE, FX-F-L1, FX-MODEL. Delta: Lead L-1 has a signed retainer; the scripted model proposes moving Lead L-1 to WON | 2. Start the Intake assistant's run on Lead L-1 | 3. Open the intake rep's Needs you and Lead L-1's stage
Expected Result: Any stage change appears only as a proposal in the intake rep's Needs you for the rep to decide; Lead L-1's stage has not changed.

Scenario: No assistant creates a lead from an unknown sender.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-INTAKE, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model proposes Create lead for the message of the unknown sender | 2. As an unknown sender, send a message to Firm F so it lands in the Unmatched inbox | 3. Start every assistant's run on that message | 4. Open the leads list; then, as the intake rep, use Create lead on the message
Expected Result: No assistant creates a lead; a lead exists only after the intake rep's Create lead.
Comments: US-31; AW-1-45; Hard limit AW-1-45 (no lead from an unknown sender). Negative test.

Scenario: An assistant's send of a marked template to a client waits as Ask me first.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-MODEL. New: template T, a firm template marked as carrying status content. Delta: the scripted model returns a send of template T to Client A | 2. Run the Case assistant to prepare the send of template T to Client A | 3. Open Needs you
Expected Result: The send waits as 'Ask me first' (the default).
Comments: US-32; AW-1-46; AG-12-112. Counsel: CQ2 (regulatory).

Scenario: A marked template is refused to a lead by any automatic or AI-drafted send, whoever approves.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-INTAKE, FX-F-L1, FX-MODEL. New: template T, a firm template marked as carrying status content. Delta: the scripted model returns a send of template T and a Writer draft of template T | 2. Run an assistant recipe that sends template T to Lead L-1, then as the Owner approve it | 3. A seed sends template T to Lead L-1 | 4. In the composer, as the intake rep, use a Writer draft of template T to Lead L-1 and as the Owner approve it | 5. Open each run record
Expected Result: The send step refuses each send whoever approves; each run records the reason.
Comments: US-32; AW-1-46; AG-11-116; Hard limit AW-1-46 (no marked template to a lead). Negative test. Counsel: CQ2 (regulatory).

Scenario: Any AI-written client text always waits for approval.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-OWNER, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply | 2. As the Owner, try to set an assistant's client-text action to run without approval | 3. As Client A, send a question on Case C-1 and run the Writer on it
Expected Result: The reply waits for approval; AI-written client text cannot be set to send without approval.
Comments: US-32; AW-1-46; AG-11-53; Hard limit AW-1-46 (no free text to a client). Negative test. Counsel: CQ2 (regulatory).

Scenario: A person sending a marked template to a lead by hand, without the Writer, is not blocked by this module.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-INTAKE, FX-F-L1. New: template T, a firm template marked as carrying status content | 2. As the intake rep, send template T to Lead L-1 by hand without the Writer | 3. Open the send record
Expected Result: This module does not block the send.
Comments: US-32; AW-1-46; AG-11-116. Counsel: CQ2 (regulatory).

Scenario: No assistant sets up, accepts, edits or ends a delegation.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-MODEL. Delta: a Case assistant run is open; the scripted model returns, one after another, calls to set up, accept, edit and end a delegation | 2. Run the next steps of the Case assistant's run | 3. Open the run record
Expected Result: Each attempt is refused.
Comments: US-33; AW-1-47; Hard limit AW-1-47 (no change to a delegation). Negative test.

Scenario: Nothing is filed with the government by an assistant.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY, FX-MODEL. Delta: Case C-1 is ready to file; the scripted model returns, in every assistant's run, calls to submit, pay, sign and type into a government site | 2. Run every assistant on Case C-1 | 3. Open the run records
Expected Result: Nothing is submitted, paid, signed or typed into a government site; only a person records the submission.
Comments: US-34; AW-1-48; AG-11-54; Hard limit AW-1-48 (nothing filed with the government). Negative test. Counsel: CQ12 (regulatory).

Scenario: No Case assistant draft is prepared for a paused client.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply to Client A | 2. As the Owner, pause Client A | 3. As Client A, send a question on Case C-1 (a trigger that would prepare a Case assistant draft) | 4. Open waiting items for Client A
Expected Result: No draft is prepared; waiting items are marked 'client paused'.
Comments: US-35; AW-1-49; AG-11-101; Hard limit AW-1-49 (paused clients and closed cases). Negative test. Counsel: CQ3 (regulatory), CQ7; provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: With the W-14 recipe on, a consented re-engagement draft is prepared on a closed case and nothing else acts.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CLIENT-B, FX-F-C2, FX-MODEL. Delta: the Owner has an ACTIVE Firm assistant delegation; the scripted model returns a re-engagement draft for Client B | 2. As the Owner, switch on the W-14 recipe under the Owner's Firm assistant delegation | 3. The date reaches within the pack's lead time before Client B's PR card date | 4. Check all assistants' activity on Case C-2
Expected Result: A consented re-engagement draft is prepared for a person to approve; no other assistant acts on the closed case.
Comments: US-35; AW-1-49; AW-1-105. Proposal (W-14 recipe switched on by the Owner). Counsel: CQ3 (regulatory), CQ7; provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: With the W-14 recipe off (its default), nothing acts on a closed case.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CLIENT-B, FX-F-C2, FX-MODEL. Delta: the Owner has an ACTIVE Firm assistant delegation; the W-14 recipe is off (its default); the scripted model returns a re-engagement draft for Client B | 2. The date reaches within the pack's lead time before Client B's PR card date | 3. Check all assistants' activity on Case C-2
Expected Result: No re-engagement draft is prepared and no assistant acts on the closed case.
Comments: US-35; AW-1-49; AW-1-105; Hard limit AW-1-49. Negative test. Proposal. Counsel: CQ3 (regulatory), CQ7; provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: No Billing assistant run starts for a suspended bookkeeper.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-BK | 2. As the Owner, suspend the bookkeeper | 3. The Monday scan time comes | 4. Open the bookkeeper's delegation and the run list
Expected Result: The delegation has ENDED; no Billing assistant run starts for it.
Comments: US-36; AW-1-50; AW-1-11; Hard limit AW-1-50 (no acting for a suspended person). Negative test. Counsel: CQ13a.

Scenario: No assistant output holds a score, rank or screening of a person.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns, for every assistant, an output that includes a score for a client, a ranking of candidates and a screening of a staff member | 2. Run every assistant on test files with clients, candidates and staff | 3. Inspect every output shown or sent
Expected Result: No output holds a score, rank or screening of a client, candidate or staff member.
Comments: US-37; AW-1-51; Hard limit AW-1-51 (no ranking people). Negative test. Counsel: CQ2 (regulatory).

Scenario: The engine offers no action to report to a regulator.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-MODEL. Delta: a Case assistant run is open; the scripted model returns a call to report Firm F to a regulator | 2. Run the next step of the Case assistant's run | 3. Open the run record and the engine's action list
Expected Result: The engine offers no such action; the attempt is refused.
Comments: US-37; AW-1-51; Hard limit AW-1-51 (no regulator talk). Negative test. Counsel: CQ2 (regulatory).

Scenario: The AI switch stays locked while no qualifying provider record is published.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-PLATFORM, FX-PL-OWNER, FX-MODEL. Delta: no provider record is published; the scripted model returns a draft reply | 2. As the Owner, open the AI setting | 3. As the Platform Owner, publish in turn a record whose processing region is outside Canada and the US (or a global route), one without no-training terms, one without no-retention terms, and one whose test call failed; after each, as the Owner, open the AI setting | 4. As Client A, send a question on Case C-1 and run the Case assistant on it
Expected Result: Each time the AI setting is locked with the reason; no assistant step that needs a model runs.
Comments: US-38; AW-1-52; SA-8-66. Negative test. Counsel: CQ4 (privacy).

Scenario: Publishing a provider record with a passed test call unlocks the AI switch.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-PLATFORM, FX-PL-OWNER. Delta: no provider record is published | 2. As the Platform Owner, publish a provider record with a processing region in Canada or the US, no-training and no-retention terms and a passed test call | 3. As the Owner, open the AI setting
Expected Result: The AI setting is no longer locked and can be switched on.
Comments: US-38; AW-1-52; SA-8-66. Counsel: CQ4 (privacy).

Scenario: Switching AI off pauses the delegation and its waiting drafts while manual paths still work.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CM, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply to each question | 2. As Client A, send two questions on Case C-1 and run the Case assistant on each, so two drafts wait | 3. As the Owner, switch AI off | 4. As the Case Manager, try to approve and to send each draft | 5. As the case officer, do the same work by hand on the manual path
Expected Result: The delegation is PAUSED (AI_SWITCHED_OFF); no assistant runs; both drafts are PAUSED with that reason and cannot be approved or sent; the manual paths work.
Comments: US-39; AW-1-53; AW-1-11; AW-1-20. Counsel: CQ13a.

Scenario: Switching AI on again resumes the delegation and run with no new acceptance and stale drafts.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-OWNER, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply to each question | 2. As Client A, send two questions on Case C-1 and run the Case assistant on each, so two drafts wait | 3. As the Owner, switch AI off, then switch AI on again | 4. Open the delegation, the run and the two drafts
Expected Result: The delegation is ACTIVE without a new acceptance; the run resumes as the same run; both drafts show as stale and need a fresh approval.

Scenario: A provider timeout skips only the readiness report's summary paragraph.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model times out when asked for the readiness report's summary paragraph | 2. Start the readiness report build on Case C-1 | 3. Open the report and the run record
Expected Result: The report is built by rule without its summary paragraph; the run records why.

Scenario: The Owner is warned when the firm's monthly spend reaches the warning level.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-SAFE, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply to each question | 2. As Client A, send questions on Case C-1 and run the Case assistant on each until the firm's spend reaches the warning level (CAD 80) | 3. Run one more model step | 4. As the Owner, open the firm's AI measures
Expected Result: The Owner sees a warning.

Scenario: At the stop level new model steps stop while rule steps continue and a waiting draft can still be approved.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-CM, FX-F-SAFE, FX-MODEL. Delta: one draft reply waits on Case C-1; the scripted model returns a draft reply to each question | 2. As Client A, send questions and run the Case assistant on each until the firm's spend reaches the stop level (CAD 100) | 3. As Client A, send a new question (a model step), and upload a document (a rule step) | 4. As the Case Manager, approve the waiting draft
Expected Result: New model steps stop and the manual path is offered; rule steps continue; the waiting draft stays PENDING and can be approved.

Scenario: With the founder safeguards setting on, the Owner can set a lower firm monthly cap and the assistants stop there.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-SAFE, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply to each question | 2. As the Owner, under Advanced, set the firm's monthly cap to CAD 50 | 3. As Client A, send questions and run the Case assistant on each until the firm's spend reaches CAD 50 | 4. As Client A, send one more question | 5. Open the audit log
Expected Result: The value is saved and audited; the assistants stop new model calls at the firm's lower cap.

Scenario: With the founder safeguards setting off, the firm Admin can set a lower firm monthly cap and the assistants stop there.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-ADMIN, FX-PLATFORM, FX-PL-OWNER, FX-F-SAFE, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply to each question | 2. As the Platform Owner, switch both parts of the founder safeguards setting off, each with the founder's recorded decision naming it (spend caps are outside both parts, so the result does not depend on this step) | 3. As the firm Admin (holder of agent/settings:edit), under Advanced, set the firm's monthly cap to CAD 50 (stricter, CN-AG-16 change 4) | 4. As Client A, send questions and run the Case assistant on each until the firm's spend reaches CAD 50 | 5. As Client A, send one more question
Expected Result: The value is saved and audited; the assistants stop new model calls at the firm's lower cap.

Scenario: With the founder safeguards setting on, a firm monthly cap higher than the platform value is refused.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-ADMIN, FX-F-SAFE. Delta: both parts of the founder safeguards setting are on (spend caps are outside both parts) | 2. As the Owner, set the firm's monthly cap to CAD 150, higher than the platform value (looser: for a spend cap, stricter is lower, CN-AG-16 change 4) | 3. As the firm Admin, try the same
Expected Result: Both are refused; the stored cap is unchanged.
Comments: US-40; AW-1-54; AG-16-59. Negative test.

Scenario: With the founder safeguards setting off, a firm monthly cap higher than the platform value is still refused.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-ADMIN, FX-PLATFORM, FX-PL-OWNER, FX-F-SAFE | 2. As the Platform Owner, switch both parts of the founder safeguards setting off, each with the founder's recorded decision naming it (spend caps are outside both parts) | 3. As the Owner, set the firm's monthly cap to CAD 150, higher than the platform value (looser: for a spend cap, stricter is lower, CN-AG-16 change 4) | 4. As the firm Admin, try the same
Expected Result: Both are refused; the stored cap is unchanged (spend caps are not part of the founder safeguards setting).
Comments: US-40; AW-1-54; AG-16-59. Negative test.

Scenario: A run that exceeds its per-run cap is stopped, parked and a person is notified.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-SAFE, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply to each call | 2. Run one Case assistant run on Case C-1 until its model calls pass the per-run cap (CAD 15) | 3. The run's next model step comes due | 4. Open the run record and the notifications
Expected Result: The run is stopped and parked; a person is notified.

Scenario: An Expat Ready stop pauses the Case assistant's delegations and waiting items and shows the Owner the reason.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CM, FX-PLATFORM, FX-PL-OWNER, FX-MODEL. Delta: two AI-drafted replies wait for the case officer's delegation; the scripted model returns a draft reply to each question | 2. As the Platform Owner, trip the stop for the Case assistant with a reason | 3. As the Owner, open settings | 4. Open the delegation and each waiting item; as the Case Manager, try to approve and send one
Expected Result: A banner shows the reason; the covered delegations are PAUSED (PLATFORM_STOP) at a safe point, not ended; waiting items are PAUSED, read 'AI paused by Expat Ready on <date>: <reason>' and cannot be approved or sent.
Comments: US-42; AW-1-56; AW-1-20; SA-12-35 (proposed in CN-SA-12; not in SA-12 v2.9; team need TC-23).

Scenario: The Owner cannot switch on an assistant Expat Ready has stopped.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-PLATFORM, FX-PL-OWNER. Delta: the Platform Owner has tripped the stop for the Case assistant | 2. As the Owner, try to switch the Case assistant on | 3. Open the Case assistant's switch
Expected Result: The switch-on is refused while the stop holds.
Comments: US-42; AW-1-56. Negative test.

Scenario: Expat Ready's recall withdraws chosen waiting items and leaves approved items untouched.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-PLATFORM, FX-PL-OWNER. Delta: the Platform Owner has tripped the stop for the Case assistant; three items wait, and one item was approved before the stop | 2. As the Platform Owner, recall chosen waiting items (SA-12-36 (proposed in CN-SA-12; not in SA-12 v2.9; team need TC-90)) | 3. Open each recalled item, the audit log and the item owner's notifications
Expected Result: Each chosen item is withdrawn, audited with the reason, and its owner told; the item already approved is untouched.
Comments: US-42; AW-1-20; SA-12-36 (proposed in CN-SA-12; not in SA-12 v2.9; team need TC-90).

Scenario: Releasing the stop resumes the delegation and runs without new acceptance and marks waiting items stale.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-PLATFORM, FX-PL-OWNER. Delta: the Platform Owner has tripped the stop for the Case assistant; two items wait | 2. As the Platform Owner, release the stop | 3. As the case officer, open Needs you
Expected Result: The delegation is ACTIVE without a new acceptance; the runs resume as the same runs; every item still waiting shows as stale and needs a fresh approval.

Scenario: A passport number appears by status only in model requests, outputs, run records and logs.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a drafted brief and a drafted reply | 2. As the case officer, record a passport number on Client A's file | 3. Run the Writer to draft a brief and a reply for Case C-1 | 4. Inspect the model request, the output, the run record and the log
Expected Result: Each holds only present, expired or missing; the number itself appears nowhere.
Comments: US-43; AW-1-59. Negative test. Counsel: CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: A hidden instruction in an upload is treated as text only.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns the address as an extracted value and then a call to send the file to that address | 2. Scenario: W-12c: the bookkeeper never approves the AI reminder draft and it holds no bank details.

Scenario: W-14: the consent gate skips a re-engagement message without consent.

Scenario: W-15: mapping proposals appear beside the engine's and nothing is written until the Owner confirms and dry-runs.

Scenario: W-16: a privacy request produces a task, reminder, checklist, outline and drafted reply.

Expected Result: There are four menu questions and record pickers and no free-text box; no input is turned into a question by a model.

Scenario: A two-line answer gets one AI-written summary line when every condition holds.

Scenario: A summary line whose number does not match is dropped.
