Scenario: The case officer asks their own assistant inline for a pickup summary.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-MODEL. Delta: the case officer lacks `agent/automation:run`; the scripted model returns a pickup summary of Case C-1 | 2. From Case C-1's screen, as the case officer, ask the Case assistant for a pickup summary | 3. Read the audit log
Expected Result: The summary is produced inline; the ask is audited as PERSON and the steps as DELEGATED with startedBy = DELEGATING_PERSON.
Comments: US-110; AW-1-124. Proposal.

Scenario: Another officer cannot ask the case officer's assistant.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CO2, FX-F-C1 | 2. As the second case officer, try to ask the case officer's assistant for a pickup summary | 3. Open the audit log
Expected Result: The ask is refused and no pickup summary is produced.
Comments: US-110; AW-1-124. Negative test. Proposal.

Scenario: Switching the Billing assistant off pauses it and leaves other assistants running.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-BK, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1. Delta: the Billing and Case assistants are on; one INVOICE_PROPOSAL waits for the bookkeeper | 2. As the Owner, switch the Billing assistant off under Advanced | 3. As the bookkeeper, try to approve the proposal | 4. As Client A, upload a document on Case C-1 (a rule step of the Case assistant) | 5. Open the delegations and the Case assistant's run
Expected Result: Billing recipes stop; its delegation is PAUSED (ASSISTANT_SWITCH_OFF); the proposal is PAUSED and cannot be approved; the Case assistant carries on.

Scenario: Switching the Billing assistant on resumes without new acceptance and the proposal shows stale.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-BK. Delta: the Billing assistant is switched off; its delegation is PAUSED (ASSISTANT_SWITCH_OFF); one INVOICE_PROPOSAL is PAUSED | 2. As the Owner, switch the Billing assistant on | 3. Open the delegation and the proposal
Expected Result: The delegation resumes without a new acceptance; the proposal shows as stale.

Scenario: Switching an assistant on while AI is off runs nothing.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1. Delta: AI is off and the Case assistant is switched off | 2. As the Owner, switch the Case assistant on | 3. As Client A, upload a document on Case C-1 (a trigger of the Case assistant's recipes) | 4. Open the run list
Expected Result: Nothing runs until AI is on.
Comments: US-111; AW-1-125. Negative test.

Scenario: An unlicensed asker's question record keeps the UNLICENSED mark and the summary never alters the lines.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO. Delta: the case officer is unlicensed | 2. As the Owner, switch AI off | 3. As the case officer, ask 'which rule is behind this item' | 4. As the case officer, open the answer and the question record
Expected Result: The answer shows with AG-14-40's three lines; the record stores UNLICENSED and the scope applied; no summary line alters or restates the lines.
Comments: US-112; AW-1-126. Counsel: CQ2 (regulatory).

Scenario: The bookkeeper ends their own delegation and its waiting match is cancelled.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-BK. Delta: the bookkeeper's Billing assistant delegation is ACTIVE with one PAYMENT_MATCH waiting | 2. As the bookkeeper, end the delegation | 3. Open the delegation, the match and the audit log | 4. As the bookkeeper, try to use the assistant again
Expected Result: The delegation is ENDED (PERSON_ENDED); the match is cancelled with DELEGATION_ENDED and stays visible in the audit; a later delegation needs a new acceptance.
Comments: US-113; AW-1-11. Counsel: CQ13a.

Scenario: The Owner withdraws an unaccepted offer.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-BK. Delta: the bookkeeper has no Billing assistant delegation yet | 2. As the Owner, set up a Billing assistant delegation for the bookkeeper and leave it PENDING_ACCEPTANCE | 3. As the Owner, withdraw it | 4. As the Owner, open the delegation and audit log | 5. As the Owner, set up a new offer
Expected Result: It is ENDED with endReason WITHDRAWN, audited with the Owner as actor; nothing ran under it; the new offer can be set up.
Comments: US-114; AW-1-6. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ13a.

Scenario: Once accepted, the Owner has no act that ends the bookkeeper's delegation.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-BK. Delta: the bookkeeper's Billing assistant delegation is ACTIVE (the bookkeeper accepted the new offer) | 2. As the Owner, look for withdraw or end | 3. As the Owner, send a direct request to withdraw the delegation
Expected Result: No such act is offered and the direct request is refused; the delegation stays ACTIVE.
Comments: US-114; AW-1-6. Negative test. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ13a.

Scenario: A key the person lost after set-up is refused at the next action and the run continues.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1. Delta: the case officer's delegation includes `agent/document:change-status` | 2. As the Owner, edit the case officer's role to remove that key | 3. Run the Case assistant's next two steps on Case C-1: first a step that needs the removed key, then a step that needs another key | 4. Open the run record
Expected Result: The first action fails the AW-1-10 check and is refused and recorded; the run continues with the step that needs another key.
Comments: §9 edge 1 (key lost after set-up); AW-1-10; BR-29. Negative test.

Scenario: A trigger while the delegation is paused opens no run and is not queued.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-OWNER. Delta: the Case assistant is switched off, so the case officer's delegation is paused | 2. As Client A, send a question on Case C-1 | 3. Open the run list | 4. As the Owner, switch the Case assistant on | 5. As Client A, send another question on Case C-1 | 6. Open the run list
Expected Result: While paused no run opens and nothing is queued; after the pause ends, the next trigger opens a run.
Comments: §9 edge 2 (trigger while paused); AW-1-11. Negative test. Counsel: CQ13a.

Scenario: While a delegation is paused the Minder still reminds the file owner of recorded dates.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1. Delta: the Case assistant is switched off, so the case officer's delegation is paused; a recorded date on Case C-1 is two weeks away | 2. The recorded date on Case C-1 nears | 3. As the case officer, open the reminders
Expected Result: The product's Minder reminds the file owner.
Comments: §9 edge 2 (trigger while paused); AW-1-11; AW-1-104. Proposal (the Lead, 11 Oct, review S3d-c c-4). Counsel: CQ13a.

Scenario: A never-accepted offer stays pending, runs nothing and is not ended by an assistant switch-off.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1. Delta: the case officer has no Case assistant delegation yet | 2. As the Owner, set up a Case assistant delegation for the case officer; the case officer never accepts it | 3. As Client A, upload a document on Case C-1 (work on the case officer's files) | 4. As the Owner, switch the Case assistant off, then on | 5. As the case officer, decline the delegation | 6. Open the delegation record and the run list
Expected Result: It stays PENDING_ACCEPTANCE and nothing runs, also after the assistant is switched off and on; after the decline it is ENDED with reason DECLINED, audited.
Comments: §9 edge 3 (never accepts); AW-1-6; AW-1-125. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ13a.

Scenario: The Owner halts someone's assistant at once by switching it off.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO. Delta: a Case assistant run is open | 2. As the Owner, switch the Case assistant off | 3. Check the run and the delegation
Expected Result: The delegation is PAUSED and its run stops running at the next safe point; the delegation is not ended.
Comments: §9 edge 4 (Owner must halt an assistant); AW-1-125; AW-1-11; AW1-D34. Counsel: CQ13a.

Scenario: No act lets the Owner end another person's delegation.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO. Delta: the case officer's Case assistant delegation is ACTIVE | 2. As the Owner, send a direct request to end the case officer's delegation | 3. As the Owner, open the delegation
Expected Result: The request is refused and the delegation stays ACTIVE; the only halts are the assistant switch, the AI switch, or deactivating or suspending the person.
Comments: §9 edge 4 (Owner must halt an assistant); AW-1-6; AW1-D34. Negative test. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ13a.

Scenario: Two officers on one case: the double-run check stops two runs of the same act.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CO2, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-REQ-X. Delta: the second case officer is on Case C-1's case team; the case officer owns the case | 2. The same act (a chase for checklist item X) falls due for both assistants' runs | 3. Open Client A's messages and both run records
Expected Result: The act runs once; the double-run check on actGuardKey stops a second run of the same act.
Comments: §9 edge 5 (two officers on one case); AW-1-18. Negative test. Proposal. Note: which officer's delegation runs depends on scope wording, §13 T6 (open); not tested.

Scenario: A reassigned case stops the old officer's run and continues as a new run under the new owner.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CO2, FX-F-C1, FX-MODEL. Delta: the case officer's Case assistant has a run open on Case C-1; the scripted model returns a pickup summary | 2. As the Owner, reassign Case C-1 to the second case officer | 3. Open both runs and the second case officer's Needs you
Expected Result: The old run stops at the next safe point; the new owner's delegation continues as a new run referencing the old run; a pickup summary (W-17) is prepared for the new owner.
Comments: §9 edge 6 (case reassigned); AW-1-19; AW-1-86. Proposal. Counsel: CQ4 (privacy).

Scenario: AI switched off and on the same day pauses and resumes every delegation with stale items.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CM, FX-F-BK. Delta: three delegations are ACTIVE (the case officer's Case assistant, the Case Manager's Firm assistant, the bookkeeper's Billing assistant), each with an item waiting | 2. As the Owner, switch AI off, then on again the same day | 3. Open each delegation and waiting item
Expected Result: Every delegation went PAUSED, then ACTIVE with no new acceptance; waiting items re-render stale and need fresh approval.
Comments: §9 edge 7 (AI off and on same day); AW-1-53; AW1-D34.

Scenario: Withdrawing the provider record pauses delegations and items until a new passed record is published.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CM, FX-F-BK, FX-PLATFORM, FX-PL-OWNER. Delta: three delegations are ACTIVE (the case officer's Case assistant, the Case Manager's Firm assistant, the bookkeeper's Billing assistant), each with a run open and an item waiting | 2. As the Platform Owner, withdraw the provider record | 3. As the Owner, check the AI switch, delegations and items | 4. As the Platform Owner, publish a new record with a passed test call | 5. As the Owner, check the delegations and items again
Expected Result: The switch locks; delegations and waiting items are PAUSED (PROVIDER_RECORD_WITHDRAWN); after the new record they resume.
Comments: §9 edge 8 (provider record withdrawn); AW-1-11; AW-1-52; SA-8-67; SA-12-35 (proposed in CN-SA-12; not in SA-12 v2.9; team need TC-23). Counsel: CQ13a, CQ4 (privacy).

Scenario: When a stop and a switch-off overlap, release happens once, only after both clear.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-PLATFORM, FX-PL-OWNER. Delta: the case officer's Case assistant delegation is ACTIVE with an item waiting | 2. As the Platform Owner, trip the Case assistant stop | 3. As the Owner, switch AI off | 4. As the Platform Owner, release the stop, then check the delegation and item | 5. As the Owner, switch AI on, then check the delegation and item
Expected Result: Both reasons are recorded; after the stop release alone the delegation and item stay PAUSED; after AI is on they are released once.
Comments: §9 edge 9 (stop and switch-off overlap); AW-1-11; AW-1-20. Counsel: CQ13a.

Scenario: On release after AI off, the no-licensed-user check still stops new client-facing preparation.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-NOLIC, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply to any question | 2. As the Owner, switch AI off, then on | 3. As Client A, send a question on Case C-1 | 4. Open the run list and Case C-1's drafts
Expected Result: While AI is off the delegation is paused; after release no new client-facing reply is prepared, because the no-licensed-user pause still holds.
Comments: §9 edge 10 (AI off and no-licensed-user together); AW-1-53; AW-1-34. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: A provider timeout mid readiness report records PROVIDER_ERROR.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model times out when asked for the readiness report's summary paragraph | 2. Start the readiness report build on Case C-1 | 3. Open the AI run log row
Expected Result: The report is built by rule without its paragraph; the run log row records PROVIDER_ERROR.
Comments: §9 edge 11 (provider timeout mid report); AW-1-53.

Scenario: An item proposed before a cap is reached can still be approved after it.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-CM, FX-F-SAFE, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a draft reply to each question | 2. As Client A, send a question on Case C-1 and run the Case assistant on it, so it proposes an item | 3. Run the Case assistant on further questions until the firm's spend reaches the stop level (CAD 100) | 4. As the Case Manager, approve the item | 5. As Client A, send a new question (a model step)
Expected Result: The approval makes no model call and proceeds; new model steps stop; nothing is paused.
Comments: §9 edge 12 (cap reached between proposing and approving); AW-1-20; AW-1-54.

Scenario: A firm cap higher than the platform value is refused at any time.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-SAFE | 2. As the Owner, set the firm's monthly cap to CAD 150, higher than the platform value (looser: for a spend cap, stricter is lower, CN-AG-16 change 4) | 3. As the Owner, repeat with a per-run cap of CAD 30 and a Practice expert daily cap of CAD 40
Expected Result: Each is refused where the firm sets it; the stored values are unchanged.
Comments: §9 edge 13 (looser value); AW-1-54; AG-16-59. Negative test.

Scenario: With the approve-all part of the founder safeguards on, a looser firm confidence level is refused.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-SAFE | 2. As the Owner, set a firm confidence level of 0.70, lower than the platform value of 0.80 (looser: stricter is a higher confidence level below which values open first, CN-AG-16 change 4)
Expected Result: It is refused where the firm sets it; nothing is saved.
Comments: §9 edge 13 (looser value); AW-1-33; AG-16-59; SA-12-37. Negative test. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: With the approve-all part on, a looser hidden share or alarm level is refused.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-ADMIN, FX-F-SAFE | 2. As the firm Admin, set a hidden share of 5 %, smaller than the platform value of 10 % (looser: stricter is a larger share hidden, CN-AG-16 change 4) | 3. As the firm Admin, set an alarm level of 95 %, higher than the platform value of 90 % (looser: stricter is a lower agreement-alarm level, CN-AG-16 change 4)
Expected Result: Both are refused; nothing is saved.
Comments: §9 edge 13 (looser value); AW-1-33; AG-16-59. Negative test. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it. Note: alarm window direction is a team and counsel question (CN-AG-16 change 4); not tested.

Scenario: With the approve-all part on, a stricter firm value is saved and the assistant reads it.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY, FX-F-SAFE, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns twenty values for the report, one of them at confidence 0.85 | 2. As the Owner, set a firm confidence level of 0.90, stricter than the platform value of 0.80 | 3. Start the readiness report build on Case C-1 | 4. As the case officer, open the item
Expected Result: The firm value is saved as a firm setting and audited; the 0.85 value is listed to open first, because the stricter firm value 0.90 governs.
Comments: §9 edge 13 (looser value); AW-1-33; AG-16-59. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: With no firm value set, the assistant reads the platform value.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY, FX-F-SAFE, FX-MODEL. Delta: no firm values are set; the scripted model returns twenty values for the report, one at confidence 0.70 and nineteen at 0.95 | 2. Start the readiness report build on Case C-1 | 3. As the case officer, open the item
Expected Result: The 0.70 value is listed to open first, and two of the 0.95 values (the platform hidden share of 10 % of twenty) are shown blank for typing.
Comments: §9 edge 13 (looser value); AW-1-33; SA-12-37. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: With the approve-all part ended by the founder's recorded decision, the firm's own values govern.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY, FX-F-SAFE, FX-PLATFORM, FX-PL-OWNER, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns twenty values for the report, one at confidence 0.75 and nineteen at 0.95 | 2. As the Platform Owner, switch the approve-all part off, recording the founder's decision | 3. As the Owner, set a firm confidence level of 0.70, lower than the platform value of 0.80 (looser, CN-AG-16 change 4) | 4. Start the readiness report build on Case C-1 | 5. As the case officer, open the item
Expected Result: The firm value is saved and governs: the 0.75 value does not open first.
Comments: §9 edge 13 (looser value); AW-1-33; SA-12-37. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: With the approve-all part ended, a firm that never set a value keeps the platform default.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY, FX-F-SAFE, FX-MODEL. Delta: the approve-all part of the founder safeguards setting is switched off and Firm F never set its own values; the scripted model returns twenty values for the report, one at confidence 0.70 and nineteen at 0.95 | 2. Start the readiness report build on Case C-1 | 3. As the case officer, open the item and the firm's safeguard values
Expected Result: The platform default is Firm F's starting value.
Comments: §9 edge 13 (looser value); AW-1-33; SA-12-37. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: A seed and the assistant triggering on the same upload give one acknowledgement and one review task.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-REQ-X | 2. As Client A, upload a document against the request | 3. The upload triggers both the seed and the Case assistant's run | 4. Open Client A's messages and the tasks
Expected Result: The engine matches on actGuardKey (the document version is the occurrence); there is one acknowledgement and one review task.
Comments: §9 edge 14 (seed and assistant same upload); AW-1-18. Negative test.

Scenario: A readiness report cannot be accepted while the client is paused.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY | 2. Start the readiness report build on Case C-1 | 3. As the Owner, pause Client A | 4. As the case officer, try to accept the report | 5. As the Owner, start Client A again, then as the case officer accept the report
Expected Result: The report is marked 'client paused' and cannot be accepted; after the client is started it can be.
Comments: §9 edge 15 (client paused while report waits); AW-1-49; AG-11-101. Negative test. Counsel: CQ3 (regulatory), CQ7; provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: Approving a stale readiness report rendering is refused.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY | 2. Start the readiness report build on Case C-1 | 3. As the case officer, re-verify a value on Case C-1 afterwards | 4. Open the report | 5. As the case officer, try to approve the old rendering
Expected Result: The item re-renders on open with the changed line flagged; approving the old rendering is refused.
Comments: §9 edge 16 (stale report line); AW-1-36; AG-11-61. Negative test.

Scenario: Approve-all with every value above the confidence level still holds one value out.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CM, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY, FX-F-SAFE, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns twenty values for the report, all at confidence 0.95 | 2. Start the readiness report build on Case C-1 | 3. As the Case Manager, open the item
Expected Result: No value opens first; at least one value is still held out for typing.
Comments: §9 edge 17 (all values above level); AW-1-33; SA-12-37. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: A Restricted value is never chosen as a holdout.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CM, FX-F-C1, FX-F-C1-READY, FX-MODEL. Delta: the scripted model returns a Reader value set of five values, four of them Restricted | 2. Start the readiness report build on Case C-1 | 3. As the Case Manager, open the item ten times | 4. Inspect the HoldoutCheck records
Expected Result: A Restricted value is never shown blank for typing; no value is stored for the comparison.
Comments: §9 edge 18 (holdout on Restricted); AW-1-33. Negative test. Proposal. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy); provisional until counsel reads it.

Scenario: Suspending the only licensed user stops new client-facing preparation and reinstating resumes it.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CM, FX-MODEL. Delta: the no-licensed-user pause setting (AG-16-58) is on; the Owner holds no licence link, so the Case Manager is the only licensed user, with an ACTIVE delegation; the scripted model returns a draft reply to any question | 2. As the Owner, suspend the Case Manager | 3. As Client A, send a question on Case C-1 | 4. As the Owner, reinstate the Case Manager | 5. As Client A, send another question on Case C-1 | 6. Open Case C-1's drafts and the Case Manager's delegations
Expected Result: While suspended no new client-facing preparation happens and the suspended user's own delegations have ENDED; after reinstatement new preparation resumes.
Comments: §9 edge 19 (only licensed user suspended then reinstated); AW-1-34; AW-1-11. Counsel: CQ1 (regulatory), CQ13a; provisional until counsel reads it. Note: what happens to triggers that arrived while suspended is §13 T13 (open); not tested.

Scenario: With exactly one form approver who is the delegating officer, self-approval is allowed and recorded.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-C1. Delta: the case officer is the firm's only holder of `agent/case:form-approve` | 2. As the case officer, ask the Case assistant to prepare a form draft on Case C-1 | 3. As the case officer, approve it | 4. Open the approval record
Expected Result: Self-approval is allowed and recorded.
Comments: §9 edge 20 (one form approver who is the delegating officer); AW-1-35; AG-7-66.

Scenario: An upload against no request still forms a verdict item, without a seed acknowledgement.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CO, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-C1 | 2. As Client A, upload a document against no request | 3. Open Client A's messages and the verdict item
Expected Result: No acknowledgement is sent by the seed and the verdict item still forms for the case officer to decide.
Comments: §9 edge 21 (upload against no request); AW-1-76; AG-11-96.

Scenario: A shared sender's address is not learned and its notice starts no Billing assistant run.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-BK, FX-F-CLIENT-A, FX-F-CLIENT-B | 2. As the Owner, mark a bank sender as shared | 3. Two notices from that sender arrive, one for Client A and one for Client B | 4. As the Owner, open the sender's record and the Billing assistant's run list
Expected Result: The sender's address is not learned for either client and does not count as verified; the Billing assistant never starts on an auto-filed notice.
Comments: §9 edge 22 (shared sender); AW-1-61; AW-1-96; AG-10-62. Negative test.

Scenario: For a lead with no case, proposed answers are shown only to holders of agent/prospect:edit.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-INTAKE, FX-F-L1, FX-MODEL. Delta: Lead L-1 has no case; the scripted model returns two proposed answers (IELTS CLB 7 and marital status single) from the lead's reply | 2. As Lead L-1 (a verified lead), reply with two answers | 3. Run the Reader on the reply, which forms a PROFILE_VALUE item | 4. Check who sees the item
Expected Result: Until SA-06 §13 item 13 is decided, the item is shown only to holders of agent/prospect:edit.
Comments: §9 edge 23 (lead with no case accepts proposed answers); AW-1-94. Negative test. Proposal (IA GI-5). Counsel: CQ2 (regulatory), CQ4 (privacy).

Scenario: A lead converted while its Intake run is open closes the run, and the Case run starts only on case.created.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-INTAKE, FX-F-L1. Delta: an Intake assistant run is open on Lead L-1 | 2. As the intake rep, convert Lead L-1 to WON | 3. Check the runs before and after the case is created
Expected Result: The Intake run closes at WON; the Case assistant's run starts only on case.created.
Comments: §9 edge 24 (lead converted while run open); AW-1-87; AW-1-69.

Scenario: A person sending a marked template to a lead by hand is not blocked and no assistant is involved.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-INTAKE, FX-F-L1. New: template T, marked as carrying eligibility content | 2. As the intake rep, send template T to Lead L-1 by hand without the Writer | 3. Open the send record
Expected Result: The send is not blocked by this module and no assistant is involved.
Comments: §9 edge 25 (marked template sent by hand); AW-1-46; AG-11-116. Counsel: CQ2 (regulatory).

Scenario: A proposed match is cancelled when the invoice is paid by hand.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-BK, FX-F-CLIENT-B. Delta: a PAYMENT_MATCH waits for Client B's Invoice I-1 | 2. As the bookkeeper, record the payment by hand so that the balance is zero | 3. As the bookkeeper, open the match item
Expected Result: The item is stale and, with the balance zero, cancelled with the reason.
Comments: §9 edge 26 (invoice paid by hand); AW-1-36; AG-11-61. Negative test.

Scenario: With no reconcile-key holder, the W-12d reminder goes to the delegating Billing-role user.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-OWNER, FX-F-CM, FX-F-BK. Delta: no one holds `agent/trust:reconcile` (the Owner and the Case Manager have lost it) | 2. The W-12d run fires | 3. As the bookkeeper (the delegating Billing-role user), open the notifications
Expected Result: The reminder goes to the delegating Billing-role user, saying no holder exists.

Scenario: On a mapping version's first use in the firm, the planned portal entry is approved, then filled with verified values only.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CM, FX-F-C1, FX-FORM-X, FX-PORTAL-P. Delta: every mapped value on Case C-1 is verified; the Case Manager acts as the representative | 2. As the Case Manager, sign in to Portal P and start assisted filling | 3. As the Case Manager, review the planned entry and approve it | 4. Start the in-session filling component's fill from the approved planned entry
Expected Result: Nothing is filled before the planned entry is approved; it is shown because this is the mapping version's first use in Firm F, lists every field, value, source and the effects before Submit, and only a holder of agent/case:form-approve can approve it. Exactly the approved fields are filled with the approved values, each recorded in mode DELEGATED with the representative as actor and the delegation reference.
Comments: Re-based 14 Oct 2026 (AIW-D135; AIW-D134): the planned entry is approved only on a mapping version's first use in the firm or when it differs from the approved form values; the approver holds agent/case:form-approve; no licence default (the approver setting was withdrawn, SA-06 v3.6 SA6-D14). AW-1-147(a), (c); AIW-D113; AG-11-54. US-130; AW-1-130 (bound field list).

Scenario: After first use, the one approval of the form values carries to the portal; no second approval.
Steps: 1. FX-F, FX-F-CM, FX-F-C1, FX-FORM-X, FX-PORTAL-P. As the Case Manager, sign in to Portal P and start assisted filling | 3. Start the in-session filling component's fill from the approved planned entry, then its read-back | 4. Open the audit log
Expected Result: No planned-entry approval is asked; the planned entry is shown and recorded, and exactly the approved form values are filled, bound to that approval. The read-back runs as usual and the audit links the fill to the form approval.
Comments: Added 14 Oct 2026 (scrum 4 reconciliation increment 3). AW-1-147(c) (i) not met, (ii) not met; AIW-D135; AW-1-83; AW-1-130.

Scenario: A planned value that differs from the approved form values needs its own approval.

Delta: Firm F has already used Portal P's mapping version once; Case C-1's form is approved by the Case Manager under agent/case:form-approve | 2. Scenario: One prepared file is counted per filing, on acceptance of its readiness report.
